title: Fast Surge Rollback Conductor — compact control surface for emergency and staged reverts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, single-surface control called the 'Fast Surge Rollback Conductor' for Redwood Console. The Conductor sits alongside the rollout timeline and provides one-click emergency revert, staged fast-revert lanes, telemetry-anchored rollback suggestions, and a lightweight simulation sandbox. The surface must be readable by non-engineering operators, provide clear cost and risk signals, and integrate with audit logs and canary metrics. This ticket covers wireframes, interactive Figma prototype, microcopy, accessibility checks, and a short heuristic test run with SRE and Product.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype demonstrates: emergency one-click revert that triggers audit modal and rollback confirmation flow
Staged fast-revert lanes support 3 phases with explicit traffic percentages and instant-swap simulation
Telemetry anchors display anomaly signals, trending error rate, and cost delta before and after revert
Prototype contains keyboard-accessible controls and meets contrast and focus order checklist
Design spec includes copy for confirmation modals, toast states, and failure recovery messaging
Links to a sample GitHub PR and an ops runbook included in artifacts
design_notes: Primary motivation: reduce MTTR during surge failures and give PMs a safe, visible control to reduce exposure
Conductor is intentionally compact to avoid visual clutter — key actions are grouped: Emergency, Soft Revert, Stage Plan
Telemetry anchors are prioritized: error rate spike, latency tail, model quality regression (from evals), and cost burn rate
We reuse existing rollout timeline colors and introduce a contextual red outline for emergency mode
Copy tone: assertive but calm. Avoid technical jargon for first-touch operators; provide an "Explain" link for engineers
Fallback behavior: if fleet capacity prevents immediate swap, surface estimated wait and suggest compatible model variants
decisions: Use a single compact panel rather than a separate modal for initial actions to reduce clicks
Require typed confirmation (type the variant name) only for full environment reverts; emergency quick revert uses a shorter two-step confirm
Show cost delta estimate in-line before confirming revert to encourage cost-aware decisions
Expose telemetry thresholds used for 'suggested rollback' and allow toggling to view raw metrics
tradeoffs: Compact surface reduces discoverability of advanced options -> mitigated by a collapsible 'advanced' row
One-click emergency reduces friction but increases risk of accidental activation -> mitigated by guardrails and two-step confirmation with visual cooldown
Including cost estimates increases cognitive load but improves decision quality; we show a short tooltip with details to avoid clutter
